newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tanker rates up slightly on fixing.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tanker rates up slightly on fixing.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering in the Middle East Gulf was good again on Wednesday and rates picked up marginally.
By mid afternoon, five VLCCs had been seen -- three finding employment to the East, one to the West and the other to Japan.
The rate of W56 for Fuji's chartering of the Evelyn Maersk, travelling AG-Japan reflected the market, shipping brokers said.

They said VLCC trips to the East had crawled up slightly to W50.75, while vessels travelling to the West could command around W49.5-50, as evidenced by Kuwait Petroleum's chartering of the Pacific Jewel.
Rates for 80,000 tonners going cross-Med rose to W98, up W3 from last done, though as high as W105 was seen, brokers said.
"Vitol's chartering of the Lucky Lady at W105 seems to be a benchmark in the Med," an Italian broker said, adding that next seen fixtures will be close to this level.
"Trading has been strong, a shortage of good quality tonnage has occurred, which has subsequently offered support to the aframaxes," he said.
In the inter-UKC sector rates were steady to a touch firmer at W95-96, due to a slight lessening of good tonnage availability in the region. No transatlantic trips were seen.
Caribbean tankers also saw an uplift for 70,000 tonners making upcoast-U.S trips where rates gained W2.5 to W145.

Rates for West Africa maintained levels of W82.5 for 130,000 tonners, brokers said, but activity was slow. By mid afternoon, Coastal's fixing of the 125,000 tonne Comor, travelling WAF-USG, was the only charter seen.
